NGC 55 in Sculptor is a barred spiral galaxy around 6.5 million light-years away, one of the nearest galaxies beyond the Local Group, seen almost exactly edge-on so that its whole disc is foreshortened into a long, bright sliver. The knotty, uneven light along its length is what gives it its nickname: clumps of young stars and glowing star-forming regions strung out like beads, with the brightest concentration sitting off-centre rather than in the middle, a sign that it is a lopsided Magellanic-type spiral much like the Large Magellanic Cloud. It is a member of the Sculptor Group and may be gravitationally bound to its neighbour NGC 300. James Dunlop discovered it from Australia in 1826; at a declination of about −39° it never rises above the horizon from Edinburgh. Data supplied by DWARFLAB, captured with DRACO using the Astro filter under Bortle 2 skies, 300s exposures at gain 120 for 1h 45m of integration. I did not physically operate the unit for this evaluation.
